title: skyBlip activation (v1)
description: How a unit gets its serial from skyblip.eu (issue #126): the JSON the browser posts to the server, and the messages each signature covers. The unit's half travels on the companion link as the challenge, register, registration and unlock frames, which link.v1.json describes and numbers, every byte string a CBOR byte string. The browser relays their fields to the server in two requests, as JSON over HTTPS: POST /activation/challenges and POST /activation/registrations, where every byte string is lowercase hexadecimal. Every signature is plain Ed25519 (RFC 8032), 64 bytes, over a message that starts with an ASCII label naming its purpose and version, followed by fixed-width binary fields in the order given, so no two messages can be read as each other: register is 'skyblip:register:v1' || Nu || Ns. registration is 'skyblip:registration:v1' || DEVICEID || Pd || Nu || Ns || server key id || release (one byte, 1 for a release build, 0 otherwise) || version, the version last because it is the one field of variable length. unlock is 'skyblip:unlock:v1' || DEVICEID || Pd || serial as two bytes big-endian || Nu. DEVICEID is the eight bytes of FICR DEVICEID[1] then DEVICEID[0], each big-endian, so its hex reads as the 64-bit value. A server key id is the first four bytes of the SHA-256 of the raw 32-byte public key. activation.v1.vectors.json holds one exchange signed with the test key, which the firmware's host suite and the server's tests both check.

public_key.description: Pd, the raw Ed25519 public key of the unit, from its seed in UICR CUSTOMER

server_key_id.description: The id of the server key the firmware is built to trust: every device build trusts skyblip.eu's server key (firmware/keys/server.pub), the host suite, the simulator and a local server the public test key of the vectors

release.description: The unit runs a release build, from a v* tag and the production image key, rather than a development build. Only told to the server, which keeps it beside the key: the air shows no difference, a development unit being a real aircraft with a real serial

serial.description: Assigned densely by the server, from 1: serial 0 would put 0x000000 on the air, which decoders read as no address. The ADS-L address is the manufacturer prefix 0x00 followed by these 16 bits, under address mapping table 58

http_challenge_request.description: POST /activation/challenges, browser to server: Nu and the key the unit trusts, from the challenge reply. Answered 201 with http_challenge_response, 422 {"error":"unknown_server_key"} for a key this server does not hold, 422 {"error":"invalid"} for a malformed nonce, 429 {"error":"rate_limited"}

http_challenge_response.description: Ns, which the server keeps with Nu for five minutes and accepts once, and R over the register message

http_registration_request.description: POST /activation/registrations, browser to server: the keys of the link's registration frame (link.v1.json), and the Ns it answers. Answered 201 with http_registration_response. Refusals, each {"error":reason}: 422 'expired' (Ns unknown, spent or older than five minutes), 422 'invalid', 422 'bad_signature', 409 'other_key' (the DEVICEID is bound to another key: the key is recorded as pending for an admin), 409 'revoked_key' (an admin revoked this key), 503 'daily_cap' (too many new units today), 503 'no_serial' (all 65535 are assigned), 429 'rate_limited'

http_registration_response.description: The serial and U, which the browser sends to the unit as the unlock command
